interpretation_policy.tradeoff_rule: A measured tradeoff requires independently supported benefit and cost; intent needs separate documentary evidence.
interpretation_policy.dominance_rule: An improvement without meaningful harm in the other measured axes is a candidate implementation improvement, not an unavoidable sacrifice.
interpretation_policy.uncertainty_rule: No observed effect is not proof of equivalence; use preregistered margins and sufficient independent units.
interpretation_policy.trust_rule: Evaluate advertised boundaries and deployment requirements separately; neither grants an excuse for violations of promised controls.

studies.title: Session ordering and cross-session concurrency

design_goal.statement: Avoid colliding session runs while permitting controlled parallel execution across independent sessions.

source.documented_fact: The queue documentation describes session serialization and a configurable global concurrency cap.

comparison.changed_variable: Supported cross-session maxConcurrent setting, with the number of independent sessions fixed.

arms.description: One allowed concurrent run across a fixed set of independent sessions.
Four allowed concurrent runs across exactly the same independent sessions, after verifying support in the pinned revision.

effective grants, external services and fixture revision except the declared variable
confounders: Provider/tool capacity can cap throughput independently of the scheduler.
Same-session versus independent-session runs change the contention boundary and are a separate boundary comparison, not this causal contrast.

hypotheses.benefit: Higher cross-session capacity increases correct goodput without breaking per-session ordering.
hypotheses.cost: More active work may increase peak resources, provider pressure and tail latency under saturation.
hypotheses.falsified_when: If capacity rises without useful throughput improvement, or ordering breaks, the expected benefit is not established.

limitations: This does not disable or prove the optimality of session serialization.
Run same-session contention separately to identify its boundary; do not combine it with a maxConcurrent change.
